description: Known answers of the fixtures added for TV-020 to TV-023 (WP-PDR-08; CM plan section 9.2; 07 sections 8.3, 9.6 and 17.3; 03 section 6.5 item X10). Every check runs on a git archive export of the commit tested, with rustos exported from the lock section 3 pin object beside it (<dir>/cwht, <dir>/rustos), offline (CARGO_NET_OFFLINE=true, RUSTUP_AUTO_INSTALL=0, MIRI_AUTO_OPS=no) and with a rustup shim that refuses installs. Procedure: docs/cm/tool-validation/evidence/rust-tv-2026-09-27.sh. The kat-target and kat-host answers stay in known-answers.json.

cov-kat.clean: --summary-only --fail-under-lines 100 --fail-under-regions 100: exit 0; TOTAL lines 13 of 13, functions 3 of 3, regions 7 of 7 (100.00 percent each)
cov-kat.seeded-gap: --features seeded-gap --text --fail-under-lines 100 --fail-under-regions 100: exit 1; exactly one line with count 0, line 6 (`1`)

seeded-gap-lcov.command: cargo +1.98.0 llvm-cov --locked --features seeded-gap --lcov --output-path <f>, then tools/measurements.py --coverage <f> (TV-021 K21-4, INSP-040 finding-2)
seeded-gap-lcov.provenance: hand-derived from src/lib.rs: llvm-cov gives a line record to each line that starts a counted region, here lines 2 (fn sign), 3 (if x < 0), 4 (-1), 6 (1), 8 (closing brace of sign) and 12 (test negative); line 15 (test positive) is compiled out by seeded-gap; the only test calls sign(-5), so line 6 is never executed: LF 6, LH 5, DA:6,0, and 5/6 = 83.33 percent

rustos-blinky.source: rustos templates/pico2 at the lock section 3 pin 2ec64c0f15c8cd2dbcaa241abffdd72f8cae467c with the three-line Cargo.toml diff of docs/vv/reports/TC-SW-TOOL-001-r3/blinky-build.txt (package name; api and pico2 as path dependencies into the export)
rustos-blinky.same_path: pass criterion (K20-4): two clean builds of the same source at one absolute path (layout A, different target directories) both exit 0 and give byte-identical ELF files and byte-identical loadable images (rust-objcopy -O binary); checked by cmp, no hand judgement
rustos-blinky.reference: docs/vv/reports/TC-SW-TOOL-001-r3/rustos-blinky.elf, ELF SHA-256 3c0ac0747a761bf9880e21f80ba613cfcb5e8f5ddddbdea7af85dbf8952bbd08, loadable image (rust-objcopy -O binary) SHA-256 c6d27ba14d7161db90244c64f129abe22cacc0a06560579be7e0c66562a831df, 2008 bytes; built on 2026-09-26 at another absolute path, so it is not a pass criterion of any check
rustos-blinky.cross_path_observation: not a pass criterion: the layout B build and the reference are compared with the layout A build and reported (loadable image equal or not; section table of rust-size -A equal or not). The crate disambiguator hashes in the symbol names (for example _RNvCs<hash>_5pico2...) are derived from the absolute path of each path dependency, and the linker places functions in symbol order, so a build at another absolute path may place main and rust_begin_unwind in a different order: equal section sizes, different bytes (TV-020 limitation 1; INSP-040 finding-1). The reference ELF is reproduced only at its own absolute path

cwht-app.reference: docs/vv/reports/TC-SW-TOOL-001-r3/cwht-app.elf (built at 0bcea39; firmware/ sources unchanged since, only firmware/unsafe-audit.md differs), ELF SHA-256 388d1d16dae55d33fcc0c69d33689abcf6d056bcc16e44a18abab2ac2300a5bf, loadable image SHA-256 828bca3546099ab8c65131c87bed5fc355208d0aade12cf315e9915c836e61f4
cwht-app.same_path: pass criterion (K20-5, MSR-28): two clean builds of the same source at one absolute path (layout A, different target directories) both exit 0 and give byte-identical ELF files and byte-identical loadable images; checked by cmp, no hand judgement
cwht-app.cross_path_observation: not a pass criterion: the layout B build and the reference are compared with the layout A build and reported (loadable image equal or not; section table of rust-size -A equal or not). The ELF differs across paths because the release profile keeps debug information, which names the build path; the loadable image was equal across paths in runs 1 and 2, which is not guaranteed, because cwht-app takes the rustos crates as path dependencies (the mechanism of the rustos-blinky entry)
